findings.rationale: From round 11 ME's feature distribution shifts (GenHlth, then AgeGroup and HighBP; per-round shift_sd near 0.9-1.0 against a pre-onset baseline near 0-0.7). Its update norm roughly doubles (about 1.3-1.6x the median before round 11, about 2.8-3.4x after) and its cosine to the median update turns negative from round 12 on. Its feature tails are also anomalous at round 20 (GenHlth p99 z_noise 6.2). Local performance is not a label problem (AUC 0.82), but CITL is flagged at z=+3.8, consistent with a miscalibrated shifted population. The pattern is a data shift that starts at round 11, not a sign-flipped or scaled upload.

MN's features shift from round 11 (GenHlth, AgeGroup, HighBP; mean_shift_sd z=+4.5 in the drift screen, onset 11). Its update norm jumps from about 1.4-1.7x to about 2.7-3.1x the median at round 11 and its cosine turns negative (about -0.09 at round 11, down to -0.75 by round 19). Its round-20 feature tails are anomalous (HighBP mean z_noise -7.7). Local AUC looks normal, so this reads as a data shift that propagates into training, not as an upload manipulation.

GA's update norm and cosine change at round 11 (norm ratio 1.75 at round 11, then 1.3-1.9 with cosines mostly negative, -0.3 to -0.7, from rounds 12-17). Before round 11 its updates track the median closely. Its features shift as well: HighBP mean is strongly depressed at round 20 (p01 z_noise -7.0), and its AgeGroup and GenHlth tails move (AgeGroup p01 z_noise 5.3, GenHlth p99 z_noise 4.6). The drift screen flags max_shift_sd z=+3.7 with onset 11. Two independent tools agree, but the shift signal is noisier than for ME and MN, so confidence is lower.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, and subgroup_outcomes by Sex, AgeGroup and Income, then used per-round follow-ups on the suspects. Three clients (ME, MN, GA) show a consistent pattern from round 11: feature distributions shift (GenHlth, AgeGroup, HighBP), update norms jump by about 1.5-2x, and cosines to the median update turn negative. I classified this as drift rather than poisoning because the local data shift in step with the updates. Their local AUCs are normal, and the pattern is not a clean sign-flip or scale. Other weak leads (GU's small-sample update and feature outliers, VI's AgeGroup drift and Sex FNR, CT and AK's single subgroup outliers, DE/NH/TN/WY/NC single feature tails, and single-round CITL outliers) are consistent with noise from small clients or single statistics and were not reported. The full 20.0 epsilon budget was spent.
